Assessment: WriteSeedAsync() (lines 33-43) builds a frozen WPF bitmap, writes it via PreviewCacheFile.WriteAtomicallyAsync and re-reads the bytes back for the mutation corpus; no redundant disk read (the read-back is the seed used by every mutation iteration, not repeated per-iteration).

RunMutations() (lines 52-93) is the fuzz driver: for each of `iterations` mutated .pv4 payloads it asserts the read either succeeds with self-consistent fields (frozen bitmap, orientation in range, positive dimensions, correct FileBytes) or throws one of the whitelisted "corrupt entry" types, and separately asserts the corpus isn't one-sided (both good and rejected occur) and that no read exceeds 2s. This is a real, would-fail oracle: reverting any of PreviewCacheFile's validation to accept a malformed header, or to leak an unexpected exception type, fails an explicit assertion here, not a tautology.

EveryTruncation_IsRejected() (lines 95-115) truncates the valid seed to every length from 0 to full-1 and asserts each one is rejected via the whitelisted exception set, then confirms the untruncated file still decodes. Would genuinely fail if PreviewCacheFile ever accepted a partial payload (the WPF-decodes-a-half-grey-preview scenario named in the class doc comment).
WriteFullAsync() (lines 117-122) is a small helper that writes bytes to a fixed "full.pv4" path and returns it; used only by EveryTruncation_IsRejected's final sanity check.
